newsitem.title: TAIWAN: EARLY TAIWAN DOLLAR EDGES LOWER, SEEN STABLE.
newsitem.headline: EARLY TAIWAN DOLLAR EDGES LOWER, SEEN STABLE.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar edged lower in early Wednesday trade on persistent U.S. dollar demand, but dealers said downside was limited due to the central bank's determination to smooth the local unit slide.
After 45 minutes at 0145 GMT, the local unit was at T$28.723 against Tuesday's T$28.718 close.
Turnover through dealers was US$50 million.
"Despite strong U.S. dollar demand, the central bank's attitude has clearly slowed greenback buying. U.S. dollar buyers will hesitate to take action," said one dealer.
A tight liquidity in the money market also would slow the Taiwan dollar's downtrend as investors tend to sell U.S. dollars to exchange for Taiwan dollars, dealers said.
A range of T$28.70-75 was seen for Wednesday.
